title: Ukraine can play a key role enabling US energy exports to Europe
gist: Russian strikes that destroyed up to 60% of Ukraine's gas output capacity in 2025 pushed Naftogaz to build four US LNG import gateways, making Ukraine one of Europe's fastest-growing US LNG buyers (381 mcm in Q1 2026 vs 456 mcm in all of 2025). The author argues Ukraine's 30+ bcm of underground storage could become a Three Seas Initiative hub for distributing US gas across Central and Eastern Europe if Washington sustains support.

insights.claim: Russian attacks on Ukraine's domestic gas production destroyed up to 60 percent of output capacity in 2025, forcing Naftogaz to rethink its import strategy.
insights.so_what: Structural loss of domestic supply turns Ukraine into a durable incremental LNG importer, adding demand to the European gas balance.
insights.quote: destroyed up to 60 percent of output capacity in 2025
insights.locator: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s domestic gas
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Naftogaz has established four gateways for US LNG imports: Poland's Swinoujscie terminal (with Orlen), Lithuania's Klaipeda terminal (with Ignitis), Germany's floating terminal at Mukran, and Greece's Revithoussa terminal via the Vertical Corridor through Bulgaria and Romania.
insights.so_what: Diversified entry points raise utilization and commercial relevance of Central/Eastern European regas terminals and the Vertical Corridor pipeline route.
insights.locator: Naftogaz has now established four distinct gateways
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Ukraine contracted roughly 456 million cubic meters of US LNG in 2025 and 381 million in Q1 2026 alone, putting it on track for a dramatic increase in annual purchases.
insights.so_what: Annualized Q1 pace (~1.5 bcm) implies roughly a tripling of Ukrainian US LNG demand in 2026 — a new growth outlet for US exporters.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: The Trump administration has robustly backed the Vertical Corridor, a north-south gas route from Greece through Bulgaria and Romania.
insights.so_what: Political backing signals continued US support for Southeast European gas infrastructure that brings US LNG north.
insights.locator: Naftogaz has now established four distinct gateways
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

themes.theme: Ukrainian storage as a regional hub

insights.claim: Ukraine has Europe's largest underground gas storage capacity at more than 30 billion cubic meters, much of it in western Ukraine near the EU border and deep enough to offer real protection from Russian airstrikes.
insights.so_what: Storage near the EU border could provide seasonal buffering for Central/Eastern Europe, dampening winter price spikes if logistics and security are solved.
insights.quote: the largest underground gas storage capacity in Europe of more than 30 billion cubic meters
insights.locator: There is a strategic dimension here
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: If logistical and security challenges are addressed, Ukraine's storage facilities could become an important distribution hub for US gas serving Central and Eastern Europe and help meet seasonal demand spikes.
insights.so_what: Creates a potential new hub dynamic in regional gas trading, conditional on war-risk; watch investment in interconnectors.
insights.locator: There is a strategic dimension here
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Ukraine's integration into the Three Seas Initiative would give it what it has long lacked: a large-scale storage partner able to absorb and redistribute US gas across the region.
insights.so_what: Links Ukraine's reconstruction agenda to US-backed regional energy infrastructure financing.
insights.quote: A large-scale storage partner able to absorb and redistribute US gas across the region
insights.locator: This is where Ukraine’s US LNG purchases
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

themes.theme: European gas market shift to US supply

insights.claim: Europe is on track to source roughly two-thirds of its LNG imports from the United States this year, putting the US ahead of Norway as the continent's largest supplier.
insights.so_what: Heavy European reliance on US LNG supports long-term offtake for US export projects but concentrates European exposure to US supply and policy.
insights.quote: Europe is already on track to source roughly two-thirds of its LNG imports from the United States this year
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Russian LNG exports to some EU member states have been rising even as Europe commits to ending Russian energy imports.
insights.so_what: Phase-out of Russian LNG remains incomplete; enforcement of the ban is a swing factor for US LNG market share.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: The Three Seas Initiative, uniting thirteen EU states from the Baltic to the Adriatic and Black seas and launched under the first Trump administration, increasingly treats LNG diversification as its central energy mission.
insights.so_what: North-south interconnectors are the policy vehicle for US LNG penetration into the region.
insights.locator: This is where Ukraine’s US LNG purchases
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Gas flows through Ukraine have reversed: for decades Russian gas flowed west through Ukraine, but now US gas is flowing into Ukraine and its storage facilities.
insights.so_what: Marks a structural rewiring of the European gas map away from east-west Russian transit.
insights.quote: Gas has now started flowing to Ukraine and into the country’s storage facilities from the United States.
insights.locator: For decades, Russian gas flowed west
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Naftogaz Acting CEO Sergii Fedorenko, appointed in July 2026, previously helped expand Ukraine's LNG imports and deepen cooperation with US, Polish, Lithuanian and Greek partners, signalling continuity in strategy.
insights.so_what: Leadership continuity lowers execution risk for Ukraine's LNG import strategy.
insights.quote: His appointment in July 2026 signals continuity rather than disruption.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson

insights.claim: Further progress is not guaranteed and requires sustained US institutional engagement, including support for Ukrainian LNG imports and integration of Ukraine's gas infrastructure into the regional energy architecture.
insights.so_what: The LNG corridor build-out is policy-dependent; reduced US engagement would be a downside risk to the thesis.
insights.quote: Further progress cannot be taken for granted and will require sustained US institutional engagement.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
